knowledge:
- key_parameters: k=Number of k-nearest neighbors to define the neighborhood; should not exceed the size of the smallest cell population ;; k_min=Minimum number of cells defining a neighborhood when using density-based neighborhoods ;; batch_min=Minimum number of cells for each batch to include in a dynamic neighborhood ;; group=The metadata column name representing batch or group labels ;; res_name=Prefix/suffix name for storing results in the colData slot ;; dim_red=Subspace to use for calculating cell distances (e.g., "PCA", "MNN") ;; assay_name=Assay slot name to use for calculations (e.g., "counts", "lim_corrected")
- alternatives: scater=For general visualization and log-normalization ;; fastMNN=For MNN-based data integration ;; limma=For linear batch effect correction ;; Seurat=For mixing metric and local structure metric ;; isi=For local inverse Simpson index ;; entropy=For Shannon entropy of batch variables
- when_to_use: Use when you need to detect and quantify batch effects in raw single-cell RNA-seq data, or when you want to compare the performance of different data integration and batch correction methods.
- pitfalls: Setting k too large can include cells from different populations, violating distance distribution assumptions ;; MNN integration assumes batch effects are smaller than biological variation; if this is violated, MNN can distort internal structures, resulting in high ldfDiff scores ;; For ldfDiff, the input list names (sce_pre_list) must correspond exactly to the batch levels.

workflows.name: quantify_and_visualize_batch_effects
workflows.intent: Quantify and visualize batch effects in unaligned single-cell RNA-seq data using the Cellspecific Mixing Score (CMS).
input: sce50 (SingleCellExperiment object containing unaligned single-cell RNA-seq data with batch annotations in colData)
workflows.stages: 1. Visualize batch distribution using visGroup ;; 2. Calculate CMS using cms ;; 3. Visualize CMS results using visHist, visMetric, visOverview, and visCluster
workflows.code:
visGroup(sce50, group = "batch")
sce50 <- cms(sce50, k = 30, group = "batch", res_name = "unaligned", n_dim = 3, cell_min = 4)
visHist(sce50)
metric_plot <- visMetric(sce20, metric_var = "cms_smooth.unaligned")
group_plot <- visGroup(sce20, group = "batch")
visOverview(sce20, "batch", other_var = "celltype")
visCluster(sce20, metric_var = "cms.unaligned", cluster_var = "celltype")

workflows.name: evaluate_and_compare_integration
workflows.intent: Evaluate and compare different batch correction/integration methods by assessing both cell mixing (CMS) and preservation of local structure (ldfDiff).
input: sce20 (SingleCellExperiment object containing integrated embeddings or corrected assays)
sce_pre_list (List of individual SingleCellExperiment objects for each batch before integration, named by batch levels)
workflows.stages: 1. Run cms on integrated embeddings (e.g., MNN) or corrected assays (e.g., limma) ;; 2. Compare mixing using visHist ;; 3. Calculate local density differences before and after integration using ldfDiff ;; 4. Visualize structure preservation using visIntegration
workflows.code:
sce20 <- cms(sce20, k = 30, group = "batch", dim_red = "MNN", res_name = "MNN", n_dim = 3, cell_min = 4)
sce20 <- cms(sce20, k = 30, group = "batch", assay_name = "lim_corrected", res_name = "limma", n_dim = 3, cell_min = 4)
visHist(sce20, metric = "cms.",  n_col = 3)
sce_pre_list <- list("1" = sce20[,sce20$batch == "1"], "2" = sce20[,sce20$batch == "2"], "3" = sce20[,sce20$batch == "3"])
sce20 <- ldfDiff(sce_pre_list, sce_combined = sce20, group = "batch", k = 70, dim_red = "PCA", dim_combined = "MNN", assay_pre = "counts", n_dim = 3, res_name = "MNN")
sce20 <- ldfDiff(sce_pre_list, sce_combined = sce20, group = "batch", k = 70, dim_red = "PCA", dim_combined = "PCA", assay_pre = "counts", assay_combined = "lim_corrected", n_dim = 3, res_name = "limma")
visIntegration(sce20, metric = "diff_ldf", metric_name = "ldfDiff")

workflows.name: comprehensive_metric_evaluation
workflows.intent: Run a suite of different integration metrics (e.g., inverse Simpson index, entropy) simultaneously using a wrapper function.
input: sce50 (SingleCellExperiment object containing single-cell RNA-seq data)
workflows.stages: 1. Run multiple metrics using evalIntegration ;; 2. Visualize the overview of all metrics using visOverview
workflows.code:
sce50 <- evalIntegration(metrics = c("isi", "entropy"), sce50, group = "batch", k = 30, n_dim = 2, cell_min = 4, res_name = c("weighted_isi", "entropy"))
visOverview(sce50, "batch", metric = c("cms_smooth.unaligned", "weighted_isi", "entropy"), prefix = FALSE)
